command:
Implement task N4 from tasks.toml: Scheduler lifecycle and reminder-cron reconciliation

Two loose ends from N2. First, create_app starts a BackgroundScheduler and nothing ever stops it: there is no lifespan or shutdown hook, so scripts/dev.sh reload leaks a thread per reload and a clean stop depends entirely on SIGTERM killing the process. Add a FastAPI lifespan that shuts the scheduler down. Second, SPEC 3 and N2 both call for cron entries for reminder rules alongside the 5-minute sweep, and build_scheduler registers only the interval job; in practice the sweep already evaluates WEIGH_IN_DUE every five minutes, so the crons are redundant. Either add them or record the simplification as a SPEC 7.1 amendment - do not leave the SPEC describing something the code does not do.

Notes recorded on this task in tasks.toml -- read these first: they may be feedback from a prior review that this run must address, not just background context.
  Recommend the amendment over the crons: a reminder that fires on a cron and a reminder that fires from a sweep are the same notification once fingerprint de-dup is in play, and one scheduling path is easier to reason about at 3am than two.

Exit criteria (every one must pass before you stop):
  - scheduler shuts down cleanly on app shutdown (test)
  - no scheduler thread survives repeated create_app/shutdown cycles (test)
  - SPEC 7.1 and the code agree on reminder crons

Constraints:
  - Touch only these paths: src/cradle/app.py, src/cradle/ports/scheduler.py, docs/SPEC.md
  - Work on branch task/N4-scheduler-lifecycle-and-remindercron; create it from the current HEAD if absent.
  - Verify with: ./scripts/test
  - Then run: python3 scripts/backlog.py  (must exit 0)
  - When the exit criteria pass, set the status of this task to review in tasks.toml. Never set it to done -- only CI and a human reviewer do that.
  - Follow CLAUDE.md. Minimal diffs, no speculative refactors, no changes outside the paths above.
